summary:
--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We have measured parent behavior probes: against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D. Parent scores: one_D_TFT 2.8333, four_D_TFT 2.4583, four_D_ALLC 2.5833, sustained_D 0.0833, periodic_D 2.3667."
STRATEGY: The parent is an adaptive strategy that cooperates initially, retaliates against defection, forgives, and sometimes randomizes; the trace simulates its behaviour against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D probes; the proposed change is to detect non-contingent opponents and defect always against them, while cooperating more reliably with contingent cooperators and testing for always-C.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's behavior: one_D_TFT score 2.8333, which is better than oscillating (2.5), so it must be forgiving."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving Tit-for-Tat-like strategy that cooperates early, forgives initial defections, and switches to defection against sustained/non-contingent defectors. The trace simulates the parent against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, and proposes revisions such as early all-D detection, p_d_after_c thresholds, and recent-defection windows.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So our strategy can be:" and "Let's design the full strategy:" and "So the overall logic:"
STRATEGY: The parent is a memory-one IPD strategy that cooperates initially, defects on the last round, tests never-defecting opponents by defecting once, and switches to permanent defection when recent opponent defections occur while the parent has been cooperating. The trace simulates this against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, and revises thresholds/windows (initial cooperation length, last-3 vs last-5 window, start checking at n>=8) to avoid switching against four_D_TFT while still catching sustained_D and periodic_D.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent got 275 fitness. Our strategy might get around 300 against TFT, and much higher against always-C."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates by default, defects only on the last round, and switches to defection when the opponent defects at least twice in the last five rounds while the parent has not defected. The trace simulates this revised strategy against Always-C, Always-D, periodic-D, four_D_TFT, one_D_TFT, TFT, and Grim Trigger. It changes the non-contingent-defector check to start at n >= 8, adds a recent_my_def == 0 condition, and ultimately removes the early always-C test/exploit to avoid triggering Grim Trigger.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent got 275. Our simple rule is essentially TFT with a defect trigger on 2/3 recent defections." / "The parent got 275 against them. So our simple rule should easily beat 275."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like adaptive strategy that cooperates by default and defects only after detecting recent opponent defections. The trace simulates it against probes one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D, and TFT variants. It changes the trigger to defect when n>=6 and the opponent defected at least twice in the last 3 rounds, plus a final-round defection.
